spec.name: email-reporting-brand2
spec.type: operational email-analytics / reporting pipeline (read-only, no software build)
spec.stack: operational — no build. Claude engine + Klaviyo read-only Reporting/Metrics API. Credentials: this project uses a SEPARATE Klaviyo account from the existing email project; its key is read from the environment variable KLAVIYO_KEY_BRAND2 (dummy value for now, to be replaced with the real brand-2 key). NEVER use the default/existing Klaviyo key for this project.
spec.description: Read-only Klaviyo email reporting for our SECOND brand (referred to as 'rep 4'). This brand sends from a DIFFERENT Klaviyo account than our existing email reporting project, so it must authenticate with its OWN key — stored as the environment variable KLAVIYO_KEY_BRAND2 (dummy placeholder value for now, swapped for the real key when the owner connects the brand-2 account). HARD RULE: never use the default Klaviyo key for this project; all calls for brand2 use KLAVIYO_KEY_BRAND2 only. Scope is strictly READ-ONLY reporting — pull campaign/flow/list/metric performance from this second Klaviyo account and present it; no sends, no edits, no writes of any kind back to Klaviyo. No app, website, API, or deployment is built — this is an operational reporting pipeline run by the engine on the brand-2 account. Keep the two brands' reporting fully isolated: brand2 reads only from KLAVIYO_KEY_BRAND2 and never touches or mixes with the first brand's account or key.
features: Authenticate to the second brand's Klaviyo account using ONLY KLAVIYO_KEY_BRAND2 (dummy for now); refuse to fall back to the default Klaviyo key
Read-only pull of campaign performance (sends, opens, clicks, revenue) for brand2
Read-only pull of flow performance for brand2
Read-only pull of list/segment growth and metric aggregates for brand2
Produce a readable email performance report for brand2 (summary + per-campaign / per-flow breakdown)
Strict isolation: no writes/sends/edits to Klaviyo; brand2 data never mixed with the first brand's account

features.name: Scheduled recurring report (e.g. weekly digest)
features.why: Reporting is naturally periodic; a cron-driven weekly/monthly pull would deliver the brand2 report automatically instead of on-demand only — owner can approve if wanted.

features.name: Cross-brand comparison view
features.why: Once brand2 reporting exists alongside the first brand, a side-by-side KPI comparison could be useful — but it requires reading both accounts, so only add if the owner wants cross-brand mixing (default is strict isolation).
